title: Global-permission session model: zero-membership Internal users can drive the shell
objective: Close the gap T-044 flagged: a zero-membership Internal user (seeded internal1, spec FR-16) got an empty memberships array from GET /me, so the SPA had no permission context at all — empty sidebar, Forbidden landing, and no way to reach Tenant Manager or switch into tenants despite holding global.view_any_tenant/tenants.*. The session model now carries tenant-less global grants end-to-end and supports cross-tenant switching per PRD 5.3.
scope: API: GetMeResult gains globalPermissions (EffectivePermissionResolver.ResolveAsync with a null tenant scope = exactly the tenant-less grants)

API: SetMePreferences accepts a lastTenantId the caller is NOT a member of when ITenantAccessValidator says Ok (member OR Internal cross-tenant grant) — same validator the tenant-context middleware uses; still 403 for plain non-members

SPA session: SessionState.globalPermissions; selectHasPermission/selectHasAnyPermission union tenant-scoped + global grants (faithful to the backend resolver, which already unions global grants into every tenant's effective set)
SPA: DefaultLanding includes global grants, so internal1 lands on Tenant Manager

SPA: TenantSwitcher offers every active tenant (GET /tenants) to global.view_any_tenant holders; picking a non-member tenant synthesizes a session membership whose permission set is the global grants, then corrects the display currency from the tenant's business rules

SPA: AuthProvider rehydrates a persisted cross-tenant lastTenantId on reload (GET /tenants/{id} + the same synthesized-membership pattern), falling back to first membership when the selection is not restorable
out_of_scope: Granting Internal users tenant-workspace permissions (leads etc.) — inside a switched tenant they can do exactly what their global grants allow, per least privilege
An 'all tenants' switcher for multi-membership users WITHOUT global.view_any_tenant (their switcher remains memberships-only)
implementation_details: A synthesized cross-tenant membership's permission set = the caller's global grants — exactly what EffectivePermissionResolver yields for a non-member in any tenant, so UI gates match backend enforcement
Tenant-scoped API calls from a switched-in Internal user pass TenantContextMiddleware via its existing IsCrossTenant path (no middleware change needed)
Display currency for a cross-tenant context starts as a BWP placeholder and is corrected via the membership-only GET /settings/business-rules read (T-044)

unit: sessionSlice: selectors resolve global grants with no active tenant (new)
DefaultLanding: zero-membership internal with global tenants.view lands on Tenant Manager (new)
TenantSwitcher: zero-membership internal sees all active tenants (removed tenants excluded); picking one synthesizes a membership from global grants and corrects currency (2 new)
integration: SetPreferences_WhenInternalUserPicksNonMemberTenant_ShouldPersist (new); SetPreferences_WhenLastTenantIdNotAMember_ShouldReturn403 unchanged and still green (plain users still rejected)
Full dotnet test QuoteIQ.slnx regression gate
e2e: Scripted internal1 flow: lands on /admin/tenants (no Forbidden), switcher lists every active tenant, switch into The Brittany works, full reload rehydrates the cross-tenant context, zero failing API calls
7-role crawl: 0 distinct API failures, permitted landing for every persona including internal1

findings.resolution_confirmed: Evaluator re-audit (iteration 2, 2026-07-14): CONFIRMED. internal-cross-tenant.spec.ts faithfully implements V-084's scripted internal1 e2e flow: land on /admin/tenants (sidebar-nav visible, forbidden-page count 0, tenant-list visible), all-tenants switcher lists non-member 'The Brittany', switch into it while awaiting the PUT /me/preferences that persists the non-member lastTenantId, then a REAL full page.reload() followed by rehydration assertions (active-tenant-name still 'The Brittany', nav-tenant-manager visible, no Forbidden) - the AuthProvider cross-tenant rehydration path that was previously unit-only is now genuinely exercised end-to-end. The >=400 /api/v1 listener is attached before loginAs and asserted empty. Selectors match TenantSwitcher.tsx (tenant-switcher/active-tenant-name and the real select/option tenant-name structure), tenant-list, sidebar-nav, forbidden-page, nav-tenant-manager - all existing production testids; none added. The V-084 negative 'force-navigate a switched-in Internal to a permission-lacking route -> Forbidden' is not in this spec but is an api.negative_tests item (Forbidden behavior is separately covered by rbac-visibility.spec.ts); the F-001 blocker was specifically the missing land/switch/full-reload-rehydration flow, which is now closed. seed-authz-e2e.sh only resets internal1's password / clears required actions - grants no permissions, so the zero-membership premise is preserved. tsc --noEmit exit 0; playwright test --list discovers the test. Live-stack run not possible in this environment (accepted limitation).
findings.resolution: Committed e2e_tests/tests/internal-cross-tenant.spec.ts: logs in as internal1@thebrittany.test (zero-membership Internal, global grants), asserts sidebar-nav visible + forbidden-page count 0 + landing URL /admin/tenants with tenant-list visible, asserts the all-tenants switcher lists the non-member tenant 'The Brittany' (removed-exclusion remains unit-covered by TenantSwitcher.test since no removed tenant is seeded), switches into it (awaiting the PUT /me/preferences that persists a non-member lastTenantId), then performs a full page.reload() and asserts the cross-tenant context is rehydrated (active-tenant-name still 'The Brittany', nav-tenant-manager visible, no Forbidden) — the AuthProvider reload path previously only unit-covered. A page-level response listener asserts zero /api/v1 responses >= 400 throughout. The T-041 personas are made loggable-in by the added e2e_tests/seed/seed-authz-e2e.sh. tsc --noEmit over e2e_tests passes (exit 0); playwright --list discovers the test. NOT executed against the live stack here (global-setup fails fast — API/Keycloak/SPA + T-041 seed not running); reproducible via: dotnet run --project QuoteIQ.Api -- seed, then bash e2e_tests/seed/seed-authz-e2e.sh, then npx playwright test internal-cross-tenant.spec.ts.

findings.description: Security review of the global-permission session model passed with no escalation path. EffectivePermissionResolver.ResolveAsync(userId, null) filters every grant path to null-scoped rows only (up.TenantId == null; role/group TenantId == null), so GlobalPermissions carries exactly the tenant-less grants and never leaks tenant-scoped permissions; this equals a non-member's effective set in any tenant, so the SPA's synthesized cross-tenant membership (TenantSwitcher/AuthProvider, permissions = globalPermissions) matches backend enforcement. SetMePreferences gates a non-member lastTenantId through the same ITenantAccessValidator the middleware uses, so a plain non-member still gets 403 (SetPreferences_WhenLastTenantIdNotAMember_ShouldReturn403) while an Internal view-any-tenant holder persists it. No privilege escalation found.
